proves.claim: phone approval envelopes hide grants, bind every action field, and authenticate native intent.

link.phone.approval-envelopes-bind-field.why: A phone approving the wrong action or seeing a grant would break the approval trust boundary.

proves.claim: only explicit new-board link replies can restore a durable reply key.

link.phone.reply-key-needs-new-board-lin.why: A stray reply must never re-key a board.

proves.claim: with canary.directPush on and the relay unreachable, a canary alert calls sendCanaryPush with the stored subscriptions.

link.canary-push-wire.on-sends-stored-su.why: Alerts must still reach phones when the relay is down.

proves.claim: with canary.directPush off the alert path is identical to today and nothing is posted.

link.canary-push-wire.off-posts-nothing.why: A new behaviour must stay off by default.

proves.claim: with relay.push on, a canary alert is sealed through an injected seal port and posted as kind and sealed to the relay push/wake through an injected post port; no alert text leaves unsealed.

link.canary-push-wire.relay-wake-sealed.why: The relay only wakes the phone; a plain alert text would reach a service that must not read it.

proves.claim: with relay.push off the alert path is identical to today and nothing is posted.

link.canary-push-wire.relay-wake-off.why: A new behaviour must stay off by default.

proves.claim: with engine.nameBehindDevice on, behindDeviceOptions returns nameBehindDevice true and a behindDevices list of device, seat and engine from the roster.

link.behind-device.on-passes-roster.why: The move must name which device is behind.

proves.claim: a roster fault leaves the options empty instead of failing the move.

link.behind-device.roster-fault-empty.why: A relay fault must not fail a local move.

proves.claim: with the setting off or unset behindDeviceOptions passes neither option and never reads the roster.
the prepareEngineMove call in relay.js spreads the behind-device options into its arguments.

link.behind-device.relay-spreads-options.why: The options only matter if the call site forwards them.

proves.claim: pullboard relay on --all prints, for each excluded board, a line naming it and the exact command that relinks it.

link.relay-on-all.names-excluded-boards.why: A silently skipped board looked like a bug.

proves.claim: relay on --all --only <name> clears that one board's exclusion and links only that board, with the way out in the message.

link.relay-on-all.only-relinks-one.why: One board must be relinkable without touching the others.

proves.claim: relay off from two worktrees of one board records one board exclusion.

link.relay-off.two-worktrees-one-exclusi.why: Worktrees of one board must not each need switching off.

proves.claim: with relay.pruneReceipts on and a fake clock, a receipt from 8 days ago is gone and one from 6 days ago stays.
a legacy receipt with no recorded time stays, and with the setting off nothing is dropped.

link.receipt-prune.legacy-and-off-keep.why: Pruning must never drop what it cannot date or when off.

proves.claim: with relay.excludeByBoard on, excluding from one worktree excludes every worktree of that board and no other board.

link.exclusion-board-key.on-covers-every.why: An exclusion keyed by checkout left sibling worktrees linked.

proves.claim: an old checkout-keyed exclusion reads as the board's, and with the setting off the keying is unchanged.
next, show and claim start no relay link (relay.js linkFile git read) - relayLinked on a checkout root runs no git.

link.order.read-commands-start-no-link.why: Fast commands must not pay for a relay git read.

proves.claim: next, show and claim start no worktree-maintenance timer or canonical() git call - the quiet set holds exactly them.

link.order.quiet-set-starts-no-timer.why: A hidden timer slowed the fast commands.

proves.claim: machine device enrollment survives a new process and refuses unrecorded or revoked recipients.

link.poll.enrollment-survives-restart.why: Enrollment must outlive a process and never trust a revoked device.

proves.claim: boardPhones and joinedComputers return the recorded engine integer, or null when none.

link.roster-engine.records-engine-or-nul.why: A missing engine must read as unknown, not zero.

proves.claim: relay.js and its sibling modules stay under the 1500-line cap.

link.relay.stays-under-line-cap.why: The file-size cap keeps modules reviewable.

proves.claim: relay.js still exports the public names importers use.

link.relay.exports-public-names.why: Importers break silently when an export goes.

proves.claim: a relay read survives one reset connection.

link.reset.read-survives-one-reset.why: A pooled socket reset must not fail a read.

proves.claim: relay resets never blindly repeat writes.

link.reset.writes-never-repeat.why: A repeated write could act twice.

proves.claim: relay read recovery stays bounded and preserves refusals, invalid bodies and cancellation.

link.reset.recovery-bounded.why: Recovery must not loop or hide a real refusal.

proves.claim: waiters on a dead owner leave exactly one holder at a time.

link.lock.dead-owner-one-holder.why: Two holders corrupt the link file.

proves.claim: a lease left by a dead holder is taken over by one waiter at a time.

link.lock.dead-lease-one-taker.why: A dead lease must not block everyone.

proves.claim: a lock left with no owner by a command that died making it is recovered once it is old.

link.lock.ownerless-recovered-when-old.why: A half-made lock must not stay forever.

proves.claim: landing admission is FIFO and stale releases cannot free a successor.

link.landing.fifo-stale-release-safe.why: Order and ownership of the landing lane must hold.

proves.claim: a landing lease expires without lending the old holder another grant.

link.landing.lease-expiry-fenced.why: An expired holder must not land.

proves.claim: ordered landing admission replays identically and a takeover fences the old invocation.

link.landing.replay-and-takeover-fence.why: Replays must be deterministic and a takeover must fence the old holder.

proves.claim: fenced landing moves never take a local or queued relay fallback.

link.landing.fenced-never-falls-back.why: A fenced move landing locally would bypass the fence.

proves.claim: with the relay unreachable, sendCanaryPush posts one sealed payload to each stored endpoint.

link.canary-push.one-post-per-endpoint.why: Each phone needs exactly one alert.

proves.claim: a failing endpoint is reported and the other endpoints still get their post.

link.canary-push.failure-does-not-block-.why: One dead phone must not silence the rest.

proves.claim: offline canary needs retain alerts and do not create a relay link or board.

link.canary-needs.offline-retains-no-lin.why: Offline alerts must not create a link.

proves.claim: canary queue counts prefer the modern summary and retain the sealed legacy fallback.
canary count reads preserve private-file and link validation without migrating metadata.

link.canary-needs.reads-keep-validation.why: A count read must not rewrite files.

proves.claim: the relay machine module reads and writes its state file through relayMachineStateFile and builds no state.json path of its own.

link.io-relay-machine-state-file.state-p.why: Without this test the relay machine could build its own state.json path again, a second home for the file the store names (#9587).

proves.claim: handOverKeys passes io.githubKeys to handOverBoardKeys, so a fake io.githubKeys answers the vouch check and no GitHub fetch runs.

link.io-relay-handover.keys-through-io.why: A module-local GitHub fetch inside the link cell could not be faked and made the cell reach GitHub itself.

proves.claim: every link-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

link.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.
